You gain a flight speed of 15 ft., or it increases by 10 ft. (optional rule at the DM's discretion; we suggest limiting this to Tiny and Small creatures you wild shape into until level 8).
You can breathe underwater and gain a swim speed of 30 ft., or it increases by 20 ft.
You gain {@sense darkvision} (60 ft.) or increase your darkvision by an additional 30 ft.
You may change the type of damage one of your attacks deals to poison or acid damage.

entries: From level 8 you may instead select two additional characteristics, and from level 14 you may instead select three additional characteristics. These Adaptive Wild Shapes override the limitations of the standard Wild Shape feature.

subclassFeature.name: Touch of Time
entries: Whenever you deal damage with a melee attack, you may select one of the dice you rolled and change its damage type to necrotic.

subclassFeature.name: Old Soul
entries: You age at half the normal rate – effectively doubling your lifespan. This increase stacks with Timeless Body when you reach level 18 (increasing your lifespan twenty-fold).

subclassFeature.name: Evolution/Devolution
entries: You learn the {@spell Evolution/Devolution|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs} spell and it is always prepared. It does not count towards the number of druid spells you can prepare each day.

subclassFeature.name: Celestial Alignment
entries: You have the ability to mimic celestial events to a limited degree. As an action, you may enact one of the following events, then must complete a long rest before you can do so again:

items: {@bold Partial Eclipse:} You may shroud an outside area of up to 10 miles in diameter in non-magical darkness for 10 minutes.
{@bold Full Lunar Phase:} You may illuminate an outside area of up to 10 miles in diameter in natural light for 10 minutes.
{@bold Constellation of the Warrior:} For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you can reroll any melee attack roll of a natural 1 once per turn.
{@bold Constellation of the Sage:} For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you can reroll any spell attack roll of a natural 1 once per turn.
{@bold Constellation of the Outlaw:} For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you can reroll any ranged attack roll of a natural 1 once per turn.
{@bold Planetary Alignment:} For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you gain proficiency in all saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Deep Hibernation
entries: You gain the ability to go into a deep hibernation at will. This hibernation lasts for a minimum of 24 hours, but has no maximum length. While in this state, you do not age, do not need to eat, drink or sleep. After the minimum 24 hours has passed, you become aware of your surroundings and can wake at any point you choose. When you wake up from your hibernation, you gain the benefits of a long rest, gain temporary hit points equal to twice your level, and can permanently change how old you appear to be.

subclassFeature.name: Glimpse Future
entries: You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws. When an ally that you can see makes a Dexterity saving throw, you may use your reaction to give them advantage on that Dexterity saving throw, so long as they can hear and understand you.

subclassFeature.name: Commune with Past
entries: During hibernation, you can learn details about your world's past. These can be details that were long forgotten and have no written history, but must have been common knowledge at some point in time. This can include things such as ancient legends, tribal rivalries, and noticeable differences between the past and the current time.

subclassFeature.name: Commune with Future
entries: During hibernation, you can learn details about your world's possible future. These details must be common knowledge for people of the time explored and are what would occur if your party were to be absent for the rest of their lifetimes. This can include things such as legends, civilisation rivalries, and noticeable differences between the current time and the future.

subclassFeature.name: Guided Evolution
entries: When casting {@spell Evolution/Devolution|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs}, if you concentrate on this spell for the full 10 minutes, the changes become permanent until {@spell Evolution/Devolution|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs} is cast on this creature again or until that creature completes a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Future Sight
entries: So long as you are not {@condition incapacitated} or {@condition blinded}, you have advantage on all attacks and all attacks against you have disadvantage.

spell.name: Evolution/Devolution
entries: By touching a creature, you can cause it to take on attributes of its ancestors or descendants. A creature may accept these changes willingly or must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you may pick one of the following changes and apply it to the creature's stat block for as long as you maintain concentration:

items: {@bold 1.} Increase or decrease the damage of all of the creature's attacks by {@dice 1d4}.
{@bold 2.} Increase or decrease the creature's movement speed by 20 ft.
{@bold 3.} The creature gains a climbing speed equal to half its movement, or its climbing speed is reduced by 30 ft. (it can be reduced to 0).
{@bold 4.} The creature gains a flying speed equal to half its movement, or its flying speed is reduced by 30 ft. (it can be reduced to 0).

{@bold 5.} Select one of the creature's attacks that cause slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage and change that damage type to poison, acid, fire, cold, or lightning, or select one of the creature's attacks that deal poison, acid, fire, cold, or lightning damage and change that damage type to slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage.

{@bold 6.} The creature gains {@sense darkvision} 60 ft., or reduces its darkvision (if it has it) by 60 ft. (it can be reduced to 0). If this creature does not have darkvision, you may reduce its maximum normal vision range to 60 ft.
{@bold 7.} Increase the creature's maximum hit points by {@dice 1d4} + 4, or reduce its maximum hit points by {@dice 1d4} + 4 (to a minimum of 1).

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you may pick another trait to change for each slot above 2nd level. You cannot pick the same trait more than once.

item.name: Ceratopsian Plate
entries: {@i Armour (any plate armour), rare (+1) or very rare (+2). Requires attunement.}
{@i Heavy sculpted armour with a horned helm and shoulders in the visage of a large ceratopsian.}

+1 or +2 armour. If you move at least 20 ft. in a straight line towards a creature and end your movement within 5 ft. of it, you may use your bonus action to strike the creature, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus and piercing damage equal to your proficiency bonus to it.
You and the creature must then make contested Strength checks. If you win, the struck creature is also knocked {@condition prone}.

activation.condition: After moving 20+ feet in a straight line toward a creature

item.name: Raptor Feather Leathers
entries: {@i Armour (any leather armour), rare (+1) or very rare (+2). Requires attunement.}
{@i A thick coat of feathers lined with leather on the inside.}

+1 or +2 armour. While attuned to this item, you have resistance to falling damage. When taking falling damage, you may use your reaction to instead gain immunity to falling damage until the end of your turn.

item.name: Dead Deity Robes
entries: {@i Wondrous item (robes). Requires attunement.}

{@i These beautiful, pristine red and black robes are the last remnants of a civilisation from millions of years in the past who worshipped a deity forgotten by all, aeons ago. They are inscribed with runes in an ancient unreadable language.}

While attuned to these robes, you have an additional spell slot of whatever your current highest level spell slot is. The level of the additional spell slot is reset and replenishes after each long rest. If you aren't wearing armour, your base Armour Class becomes 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

item.name: Automimicry Cape
entries: {@i Wondrous item (cape).}

{@i This large cape is dull on the back, but the inside is patterned and coloured with two huge eyes. When held up from either side, it gives the wearer the superficial image of a huge bestial head with glaring eyes.}
While wearing this cape, as a bonus action you can give yourself advantage on {@skill Intimidation} checks until the end of your turn against any creature with an Intelligence score of 5 or lower.

activation.condition: Gain advantage on Intimidation checks against creatures with INT 5 or lower

item.name: Pterosaur Wingbow
entries: {@i Weapon (any bow). Requires attunement.}

{@i This slender bow is made from pterosaur bones and stringed with a fine muscle tendon. The tendon can magically extend into a full wing membrane, connecting and wrapping the bones to form a gliding wing.}

+2 weapon. As a bonus action, the bow can be unfurled into a gliding wing, allowing the wielder to descend safely from any height, so long as they are not {@condition incapacitated}. Additionally, they may glide 2 ft. in any horizontal direction for every 1 ft. they descend, without using any movement.

item.name: Kriss of Haţeg
entries: {@i Weapon (dagger or knife). Requires attunement.}
{@i This slender weapon has a wavy oscillating blade engraved with strange symbols.}

+3 weapon. A creature hit by an attack with this weapon must succeed a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or be reduced by one size category and have the damage from its attacks reduced by {@dice 1d4} for 1 minute. While reduced in size, it cannot be reduced in size again by another attack or similar spell/ability.

activation.condition: When you hit a creature with this weapon

item.name: The Taming Rod
entries: {@i Weapon (polearm or spear). Requires attunement.}
{@i A long pole with a bladed steel tip and a hooped ring of rope dangling from the end. A line of rope then runs parallel to the shaft and can be pulled to open or close the hoop.}
+1 weapon. While attuned to this weapon, you may attempt to tame an animal an additional time per day (either the same animal or a different one, see page 232).

item.name: Razortooth Sword
entries: {@i Weapon (any sword), uncommon, rare (+1), very rare (+2), or legendary (+3). Requires attunement if rare or rarer.}
{@i This gnarled sword is covered in sharp teeth embedded into its cutting edge.}

A creature hit by an attack with this weapon gains one level of Bleed Effect, as described below. The bonus conveyed by +1/+2/+3 versions of this weapon do not increase the damage this weapon deals when hitting, but instead add additional levels of Bleed Effect equal to the weapon's bonus (i.e. a +1 sword applies a total of 2 levels of Bleed Effect per hit).

items: A creature with this effect suffers 1 slashing damage at the start of its turn in combat for each level of bleed effect it has.
Outside of combat, a creature suffers 1 slashing damage every minute for each level of bleed effect it has, so long as it is not taking a short or long rest.
One level of bleed effect is removed per hit point of healing received.

All bleed effects can be simultaneously removed by completing a short or long rest, being restored to full health, or by a successful {@skill Medicine} check ({@dc 6} + level of bleed effect, to a maximum of 15).

item.name: Barron's Blunderbuss
entries: {@i Weapon (musket or hunting rifle), uncommon, rare (+1), very rare (+2), or legendary (+3). Requires attunement if rare or rarer.}
{@i A metal trumpet-like gun with a wide nozzle and bespoke wooden handle.}

This weapon can be loaded with any type of ammunition, or alternatively pebbles, scrap, or any cluster of small items you desire. However, its range becomes 60 ft. if you do so. Additionally, a DM can alter the damage type of this weapon to match what it is loaded with (i.e. putting a large rock in could change the damage to bludgeoning, or icicles could change it to cold damage).

item.name: Trusty Rusty
entries: {@i Weapon (warpick). Requires attunement.}
{@i This worn pick is rusted and corroding, but still maintains a sharp point.}
+3 weapon. While wielding this weapon, you gain a burrowing speed of 5 ft. Additionally, you have advantage on attacks against creatures made of rock or stone.

item.name: Protoceratops Quillbow
entries: {@i Weapon (any crossbow).}
{@i This wooden crossbow's end is carved into the beaked-mouth of a Protoceratops and its frill forms the crossbow's sights.}

This weapon's bolts detonate with tiny spines on impact. When a creature is hit by an attack made with this weapon, {@damage 1d4} piercing damage is inflicted to each creature within 5 ft. of the hit target.

item.name: Geological Hammer
entries: {@i Weapon (any hammer or one-handed mace).}
{@i This hammer has a broad flat head, and the back of the hammer is pointed into a triangular edge.}
In addition to its use as a weapon, this item can be used as a tool to efficiently extract resources from rock.

item.name: Theropod Jaw
entries: {@i Weapon (greataxe), uncommon, rare (+1), or very rare (+2). Requires attunement if very rare.}
{@i This huge axe is crafted from the harvested jaw of a mighty predatory dinosaur.}
This weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d6} piercing damage with each successful hit.

item.name: Azdarchid Beak Greatsword
entries: {@i Weapon (greatsword).}
{@i This lightweight sword is crafted from the huge beak of an Azdarchid pterosaur. It can slide through the air with ease.}

When using your reaction to make an attack of opportunity with this weapon, your melee reach is increased to 10 ft. for that attack. Furthermore, attacks made with this weapon against creatures from the elemental plane of air are made at advantage.

item.name: Sauropod Femur
entries: {@i Weapon (maul or mace).}
{@i This bony mace is topped with a large bulbous head. Despite its size, it is remarkably light.}
This weapon weighs half as much as it usually would, but is just as effective.

item.name: Wand of the Wondering Mind
entries: {@i A simple, wooden wand bound with twine and a small feather embedded in its tip.}

This wand has 3 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges and a beast you can see within 40 ft. of you must make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, select a Behaviour Table (pages 214–217). You may then roll two dice for a behaviour and select whichever option of the two you prefer. The creature then behaves in that manner.
This wand regains all expended charges every day at dawn.

item.name: Refractive Index Crystal
item.reqAttune: by a druid, wizard, or sorcerer
entries: {@i Wondrous item (spell focus), uncommon (+1, "Exceptional"), rare (+2, "Flawless"), or very rare (+3, "Perfect"). Requires attunement by a druid, wizard, or sorcerer.}
{@i This large, jagged crystal has a pastel colour hue to it, but when turned in light it refracts brilliant rainbows.}

This item can be used as a spell focus by a druid, wizard, or sorcerer. While wielding this item, you may cast the {@spell light} cantrip a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per day, and you may cast the spell {@spell colour spray} at 1st level once per day without using a spell slot.

item.name: Ancient Horn
entries: {@i Wondrous item (instrument).}
{@i A curved and polished bone horn made from the skull of a large hadrosaur.}

This instrument can be used as a spell focus by a bard. Once per day, as an action, the horn can be blown to alert allies. When used in this way, it cannot be heard by anyone except the bearer and their allies, who can hear it regardless of where they are in the multiverse. The sound itself does not convey specific information, and is simply a deep note.

item.name: Primal Drums
entries: {@i Wondrous item (instrument).}
{@i A small set of palm drums that are fashioned traditionally from skin stretched over hollowed wood.}
This instrument can be used as a spell focus by a bard. Once per day, as an action, these drums can be used to cast the spell {@spell bless} at 1st level without requiring a spell slot or components.

item.name: Staff of Time Sight
entries: {@i Weapon (quarterstaff). Requires attunement.}

{@i This wooden and brass staff is topped by a large, spinning brass sphere. This sphere is orbited by several smaller brass spheres that are not physically connected to the staff, yet cannot be removed from their orbit.}

This +2 staff can be used as a spell focus by a druid, wizard, or sorcerer. This staff has two charges. While wielding this staff, at the end of your turn in combat, you may choose to expend 1 of its charges. If you do, undo your entire turn (all actions, movement, and damage dealt/received) and re-take your turn. The staff regains 1 charge each day at dawn.

activation.condition: During combat, undo your entire turn and retake it

item.name: Staff of Unspared Expense
entries: {@i Weapon (quarterstaff), cursed. Requires attunement.}
{@i This pale ivory-coloured staff is topped with a piece of polished amber that contains a large insect fossil.}
This +3 staff can be used as a spell focus by a druid, wizard, or sorcerer. While wielding this staff, you have advantage on all Charisma checks and Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Curse
entries: While in possession of this staff, all vendors try to sell their wares at prices 50% more expensive than normal to you. This staff is cursed and, once attuned, a player cannot unattune to it. If they were to abandon the staff, it appears among their belongings during the next short or long rest. The curse can be broken by selling the staff at 200% of its usual value (DM's choice).

Alternatively, the curse can be broken by destroying the staff by succeeding on a {@dc 25} Strength check. If the staff is destroyed in this manner, a blinding flash of light emits from the shattered amber, then heavy and intermittent stomping footsteps can be heard in the distance that steadily grow louder. This is the sound of a young/adult/ancient Tyrannosaurus rex approaching (age depends on the party level, at DM's discretion). It is hostile to the party, cannot be tamed, and will pursue them as long as it can. It will actively hunt them if the party escapes.

item.name: Amber Necklace
entries: {@i A simple twine necklace binding a small lump of amber, or a chain of amber beads.}
While wearing this necklace, you have a +2 bonus to any roll to resist or end the {@condition poisoned} condition. This effect is not cumulative with further amber items.

item.name: Ring of Primal Speaking
entries: {@i This small gold ring has the visage of a toothed maw biting onto a gemstone.}
While wearing this ring, you can read, speak, and understand Archosauric.

item.name: Ring of Palaeobotany
entries: {@i This wooden ring has a large emerald inlay. Within the emerald is a single tiny golden leaf.}
While wearing this ring you are able to recognise all ancient plants (that existed before your original timeline/lifespan) and you have knowledge of their uses and dangers.

item.name: Evolunite Shard
entries: {@i A tiny shard of iridescent rock that sparkles when in moonlight. When it comes into contact with a creature's integument (skin/scales/feathers/hair/etc.), it sparks and sizzles as it dissolves into them.}

If this mineral touches a creature's exposed body, it is destroyed. The DM then rolls on the Minor Mutation Table (page 218) for that creature, and it gains the associated mutation for 1 hour. If more than five Evolunite shards are used on the same creature within 1 hour of each other, the creature is {@condition polymorphed|phb|polymorphed} into a tiny crab with 2 hit points for 1 hour.

item.name: Potion of Redirected Ancestry
entries: {@i This ornate glass vial is inlaid with gold filigree. It contains a dully-glowing, green liquid that has tiny double helix shapes drifting within it.}

Consuming this potion allows you to take on the appearance and abilities of any humanoid race/species that you share a common ancestor with. These replace your character's original racial/species abilities and appearance. This effect lasts for 1 hour, however if you drink a second Potion of Redirected Ancestry while under this effect, the change becomes permanent unless removed by a {@spell wish} spell.

item.name: Potion of Plumage
entries: {@i This simple vial is filled with feathers immersed in a strange blue liquid.}

When this potion is consumed, the creature that drank it sprouts soft downy feathers all over their body and long flight feathers from their forearms for 10 minutes. While under this effect, they take no damage from falling and are able to glide 1 ft. horizontally for every 1 ft. they descend while falling.

item.name: Ethereal Egg
entries: {@i This football-sized egg is partly translucent, and wisps of coloured smoke constantly drift off of it.}

If incubated (kept warm) for {@dice 2d4} days, the egg will hatch into a familiar for the player who incubated it last. This functions in the same manner as a familiar would via the {@spell find familiar} spell, with the following exceptions:

items: The familiar's appearance and stats are selected by the hatching player from a list of known familiars (we recommend one of the Mesozoic familiars from this book), and then cannot be changed.
Once the familiar drops to 0 HP, it disappears and can be resummoned as an action.

Once the familiar drops to 0 HP for the third time, instead of disappearing, it reverts back to its Ethereal Egg form and must be incubated for a further {@dice 2d4} days before re-hatching as the same familiar.

item.name: Shell Coin
entries: {@i This shell has been carved into a small disc. It retains many of the surface features of the shell, including ribbing and growth lines.}

When entering a settlement of 100 inhabitants or more, this shell takes on the appearance of the highest value coin for that settlement. A {@dc 12} Arcana check can determine that the coin is magical, but an effect that dispels magic is required to reveal its illusion.

item.name: Dice of the Dinosaur
entries: {@i This six-sided die has the visages of six different large dinosaurs carved into each face. Once rolled, a strange bellowing noise can be heard in the distance.}

The first time that this die is rolled each day, it summons a dinosaur that matches the carved visage of the face it rolls to. The dinosaur is summoned somewhere within a 1 mile radius and is hostile to whoever rolled the die, actively seeking them out.

If the dinosaur is slain, it disintegrates into amber gemstones worth 100 gp multiplied by the corresponding number below. Once that dinosaur has been slain, the corresponding facing on the die turns blank and becomes weighted in a way that it cannot roll with that side face-up. At the next dawn, if the dinosaur is alive, it vanishes and the die remains unchanged.

item.name: Large Howdah
entries: Ornate carriages built to be mounted on large creatures, functioning as mobile bases of operations that allow riders to rest while on the move and store items in a relatively safe place.

A standard howdah has a maximum capacity of five humanoids and includes two hammocks with space for two bedrolls underneath, accompanied by two storage chests, and finally a saddle with reins for controlling the mount. A creature equipped with a howdah has its speed reduced by 5 ft., to a minimum of 5 ft.

A large howdah can be constructed for 2,000–2,500 gp in 2 days by a team including a carpenter, blacksmith, and general labourers, or bought pre-built for 3,000 gp. See {@variantrule Howdahs|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs} for amenities and further details.

item.name: Huge Howdah
entries: Ornate carriages built to be mounted on huge creatures, functioning as mobile bases of operations that allow riders to rest while on the move and store items in a relatively safe place.

A standard howdah has a maximum capacity of five humanoids and includes two hammocks with space for two bedrolls underneath, accompanied by two storage chests, and finally a saddle with reins for controlling the mount. A creature equipped with a howdah has its speed reduced by 5 ft., to a minimum of 5 ft.
A huge howdah can be augmented with up to two additional amenities.

A huge howdah can be constructed for 5,000–7,500 gp in {@dice 1d3 + 1} days by a team including a carpenter, blacksmith, and general labourers, or bought pre-built for 9,000 gp. See {@variantrule Howdahs|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs} for amenities and further details.

item.name: Gargantuan Howdah
entries: Ornate carriages built to be mounted on gargantuan creatures, functioning as mobile bases of operations that allow riders to rest while on the move and store items in a relatively safe place.

A standard howdah has a maximum capacity of five humanoids and includes two hammocks with space for two bedrolls underneath, accompanied by two storage chests, and finally a saddle with reins for controlling the mount. A creature equipped with a howdah has its speed reduced by 5 ft., to a minimum of 5 ft.
A gargantuan howdah can be augmented with three or four additional amenities, or more on the largest creatures.

A gargantuan howdah can be constructed for 7,500–10,000 gp in {@dice 3d4} days by a team including a carpenter, blacksmith, and general labourers, or bought pre-built for 15,000 gp. See {@variantrule Howdahs|DrDhrolinsDictionaryofDinosaurs} for amenities and further details.

activation.condition: On a hit with a ranged attack against a Large or larger creature
When you make a ranged weapon attack
When you make a ranged weapon attack
When you make a ranged weapon attack
When you reduce a Favoured Enemy to 0 hit points
During a long rest, using harvested bones
When you deal damage, you may change one damage die to necrotic
When an ally within 30 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw
While you have a creature grappled
When a creature moves within 5 feet of you while you are sleeping or resting
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack

table.name: Behaviour: Small and Medium Carnivore
intro: In fantasy games, worlds are typically populated by monstrous creatures behaving in ways that real animals don't. It's extremely rare for a real animal to attack on sight and fight to the death without ever considering fleeing, yet this is how the vast majority of roleplaying encounters play out. To better emulate realistic behaviour, you may use the tables here. These are designed to give approximations of behaviour that real dinosaurs exhibited, albeit designed in a way so that they can still be an interesting roleplaying encounter. You may roll or select the results and they may apply to an individual creature or a whole species. These tables are separated into carnivores and herbivores. If your chosen creature is an omnivore, you may pick any appropriate table.

{@b Fleeing Creatures.} Many creatures will attempt to flee when threatened. If a creature escapes the battle and the players wish to track it down, roll opposing {@skill Survival} checks. Players may only attempt this once per fleeing creature.
rows: {@b Asleep.} The creature is asleep. If awoken by a failed {@skill Stealth} check (with a DC equal to the sleeping creature's passive Perception), treat this result as a 4-5.

{@b Skittish.} The creature will attack for one round, then attempt to flee. If this creature is present in numbers equal to or greater than the party, or if it is larger than every party member, treat this result as an 8 instead.
{@b Defensively fearful.} The creature will attempt to intimidate the players and attack if provoked. If it is reduced to half health or less, it will attempt to flee.
{@b Aggressively territorial.} The creature attempts to intimidate the party. If they attack it, or do not leave, it will attack and fight to the death.
{@b Opportunistic feeder.} The creature attacks, attempting to kill and devour the players. It will only attempt to flee if near death.

table.name: Behaviour: Ambush Carnivore
footnotes: Some carnivores may be largely stationary ambush predators (similar to modern crocodiles). For those creatures, we suggest you use the ambush table when putting them in your world.
rows: {@b Waiting in ambush.} The creature uses any abilities it has to keep entirely hidden, attacking at anything (other than its own species) that comes within half of its walking speed. It will cease attacking and flee, attempting to hide again if near death.
{@b Basking.} The creature is conspicuously visible, basking in the sun to warm itself. It will only attack if threatened and will attempt to flee if reduced to below half health.
{@b Patrolling territory.} The creature is actively patrolling its hunting or mating grounds. It will attack and fight to the death anything it encounters but won't pursue them if they flee.

table.name: Behaviour: Large Carnivore
rows: {@b Asleep.} The creature is asleep. If awoken by a failed {@skill Stealth} check (with a DC equal to the sleeping creature's passive Perception), treat this result as an 8.

{@b Rest and digest.} The creature is aware of the party, but cares little and has already fed. If they come within 10 ft. of it, it will attempt to intimidate them and will only attack if they touch it or attack it.

{@b Irritable.} The creature will attempt to drive the players away with an intimidating threat display. If they don't leave or if they attack, it will fight back. It will only attempt to flee if near death. If it escapes, it will recover to full strength (complete a long rest) and then actively hunt the players.

{@b Territorial challenge.} The creature perceives the party's intrudance as a challenge. It attempts to intimidate the party once, then immediately attacks if the players do not flee. It will fight to the death.

{@b Actively hunting.} The creature attacks the players, only fleeing if near death. It will focus on the weakest-looking member of the party. If the party escapes, it will continue to pursue them as long as it is able. To track the players, the creature must roll a contested {@skill Survival} check vs the party member with the lowest survival modifier. Abilities that cover the party's track (such as a Ranger's {@spell Pass Without Trace}) renders the creature unable to track the party.

table.name: Behaviour: Large Herbivore
intro: The behaviour of a herbivore that can flee a predator (i.e. a Gallimimus) and one that can't (i.e. an Ankylosaurus) is very different when threatened. Use your own judgement when determining whether a creature is 'fast' or 'slow', but we recommend treating any herbivore with a walking speed of 20 ft. or less as 'slow'. For very large and slow sauropods, you can roll on either the Large Herbivore or Armoured/Slow Herbivore tables.
rows: {@b Oblivious.} The sheer size of this creature makes the party seem like little more than pests. It will only attack if they attack it first. Ignore this result if anything in the party is the same size category as this creature.
{@b Fearful.} The strangeness of the party intimidates this creature. It avoids them if possible and flees if they approach.
{@b Challenged.} The creature will make a threat display, attempting to intimidate the party. If approached or attacked, it will fight to the death.

{@b Rutting.} Select either oblivious or fearful and apply that result to all members of this species in this encounter, bar one or two (or more depending on population size) individuals. Those exceptions are rutting and will attack the party. They will knock players {@condition unconscious}, but not purposely kill them. They will submit and cease attacking if reduced to below half hit points. If there are two or more rutting creatures of the same species, they will prioritise attacking each other first.

table.name: Behaviour: Armoured/Slow Herbivore
rows: {@b Immutable defence.} This creature trusts its defences and ignores the party. It will only attack if it is attacked first. If the attacker ceases attacking, so too will this creature.
{@b Stand ground.} The creature makes a show of strength, stomping and posturing. It will attack if approached or attacked. However, it will not pursue a fleeing target.
{@b Push back.} The creature immediately charges the party on sight, letting out an angry cry. It will attack until the opponent dies or flees, but will not pursue a fleeing target.

table.name: Behaviour: Small and Medium Herbivore
rows: {@b Skittish.} The creature will attempt to flee and only attack if trapped or immobilised.
{@b Frozen.} The creature will stay motionless until attacked. It will then either flee or fight, fleeing when near death.
{@b Backed into a corner.} The creature will fight to the death.

table.name: Minor Mutation
intro: Below are tables outlining genetic or magical mutations that you can use to make your creatures more flavourful, interesting, or simply more challenging. These mutations could represent regional variations of species, or perhaps the experiments of a mad wizard. You may select or roll for mutations on the tables below. One or more of these could be applied to an individual creature, a group of creatures (i.e. a pack or herd), or for a creature's entire species in your world.
Many of these mutations can be used to re-flavour a creature to fit in a particular environment, and we have indicated which environments match which mutation.

Many of these mutations make the creature more resilient or dangerous, sometimes by a significant amount depending on its initial stat block. We recommend increasing the CR of a mutated creature by between 0, ½, or 1 for minor mutations and 2 or 3 for major mutations, although some mutations may only increase a creature's CR under certain circumstances (e.g., #2 "Extended apnea" only poses an increased threat while fighting underwater). To ensure that these mutations scale with CR, we've included some that utilise stat bonuses and proficiency bonuses (abbreviated to "PB") to calculate save DCs, hit bonuses, and damage. Ultimately, how you balance these changes is up to your discretion, so if you find that these mutations are over/underwhelming in some situations, please do adjust them to fit your needs.
rows: {@b Tusked} – {@i Two bulbous teeth protrude from this creature's lower jaw.}
If this creature hits with an attack that uses its head, the hit creature must succeed a DC (8 + Strength bonus + PB) Strength saving throw or take an additional {@dice 1d6} + PB piercing damage.
{@b Extended apnea} – {@i High-capacity lungs allow this creature to hold its breath for a prolonged period.}
This creature may hold its breath for up to an hour with no detrimental side-effects.
{@b Symbiotic} – {@i This creature lives benevolently among another species.}

Select another non-humanoid creature. All creatures of that species treat this creature as an ally. Additionally, this creature gains proficiency in all ability checks while within 5 ft. of the selected creature.
{@b Diminutive size} – {@i This creature is particularly small.}
Decrease the size category of this creature by one stage (to a minimum of Tiny), decrease any damage it deals by 2 (to a minimum of 1), but add +2 to its Dexterity saving throws.
{@b Rapid coagulation} – {@i Blood oozing from wounds instantly clots when exposed to air.}
This creature cannot lose more than one third of its HP in a single turn from any combination of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage.
{@b Elongate} – {@i The limbs, tail, or muzzle of this creature are particularly long.}
Select one melee attack this creature has and increase its range by 5 ft.
{@b Vivid plumage} – {@i Beautifully coloured feathers or fur cover this creature's body.}
This creature has advantage on any Charisma checks.
{@b Thermal vision} – {@i Fleshy red spots on this creature's head allow it to detect heat.}
This creature can see other creatures while in any light level but struggles to distinguish them from other heat sources (such as torches).
{@b Pachycephalisation} – {@i The skull of this creature is huge and bulbous, giving it bony nodules that it can use as a weapon.}

If this creature moves at least 20 ft. towards a creature, it can use its bonus action to make a skull bash attack. If that creature is within 5 ft., it must succeed a DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or take {@dice 1d6} + PB bludgeoning damage.
{@b Reinforced muscle fibres} – {@i Metallic fibres line this creature's muscles.}
This creature has advantage on Strength saving throws.
{@b Prehensile tail} – {@i This creature can control its tail as though it were a limb, grasping or attacking with it.}

This creature can use its bonus action to attack a creature within 5/10 ft. (DM's choice). That creature must succeed a DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or take {@dice 1d6} + PB bludgeoning damage.
{@b Alopecia} – {@i All feathers, hair, and scales fall away from this creature, leaving only bare skin.}
This creature is vulnerable to slashing damage. Instead of increasing its CR with this mutation, reduce it.
{@b Digital pads} – {@i Soft cat-like paw pads cover the soles of this creature's feet.}
This creature makes no sound when it moves. Once per day, the first time it fails a {@skill Stealth} check, it may instead choose to pass.
{@b Hypertrophy} – {@i Huge, bulging muscles cover this creature's body.}
This creature has advantage on Strength checks.
{@b Spinnerets} – {@i Silk-producing glands protrude from this creature's body, allowing it to spin webs quickly.}
This creature may cast {@spell web} at 2nd level (spell save DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB)) without components and without requiring a spell slot.
{@b Aquatic} – {@i This creature has webbed hands and feet, as well as gills on its neck.}
This creature gains a swim speed equal to its walking speed and may potentially breathe underwater (DM's choice).
Swamp/Wetland, Ocean/Deep Water, River/Lake, Coastal/Estuary, Island/Archipelago
{@b Thermal sink} – {@i A specialised organ in this creature's chest is able to absorb heat.}
As a bonus action, all other creatures within 5 ft. must succeed a DC (8 + Constitution bonus) Constitution saving throw or take {@dice 1d4} + PB cold damage.
{@b Toxic secretions} – {@i Poisons seep through this creature's skin or scales.}
When hit by a melee attack, this creature may use its reaction to deal {@dice 1d6} + PB poison damage to the attacking creature.
{@b Sail-backed} – {@i A row of tall skin-covered bony protrusions line this creature's back, linking to form a sail.}
This creature gets +2 to {@skill Intimidation} checks and is unaffected by temperatures as high as 40°C Celsius (104°F Fahrenheit).
{@b Bristle-backed} – {@i Large quills or spines protrude from this creature's back.}

In addition to any other attack, this creature may make one ranged attack with the profile: Bristle Shot. {@atk rw} range, 30 ft., +(Dexterity bonus + PB) to hit, one target. {@h}{@dice 1d6} + PB piercing damage.
{@b Puffable coat} – {@i This creature can puff itself up with a thick fluffy coat of fur or feathers.}

When hit by an attack or when failing a saving throw, this creature may use its reaction to reduce incoming cold damage by {@dice 1d6} + PB. This creature is unaffected by temperatures as low as -20°C Celsius (-4°F Fahrenheit).
{@b Photosynthetic} – {@i This creature has a vibrant green colour, as it's skin, hair, or feathers contain plant-like cells.}
This creature requires only a few hours of sunlight for a full day's nourishment. It also counts as a plant for the purposes of spells and abilities that target plants.
{@b Floral mimicry} – {@i This creature's features look remarkably plant-like. Small frills of skin and feathers mimic leaves and flowers.}
While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from plant life. A DC (8 + Charisma bonus + PB) {@skill Nature} or {@skill Investigation} check (your choice) will reveal that this is a creature.
{@b Septic saliva} – {@i A noxious smell emanates from this creature's mouth, as it contains a horrible mixture of dangerous bacteria.}
Add {@dice 1d6} necrotic damage to any attack made by this creature that involves its mouth.
{@b Stem cell reservoir} – {@i A specialised organ holds a cluster of blank cells that can rapidly redeploy, re-growing any damaged body part.}
Once per day as an action, this creature may recover up to one third of its hit points.
{@b Bioluminescent} – {@i Some part, or all, of this creature's body glows beautifully with vibrant colours while in the dark.}
This creature emits a dim hue of light in a 15 ft. radius when in the dark.
{@b Club-tail} – {@i This creature's tail ends in a bony mass that it can use to bash targets.}
As a bonus action, this creature may make one melee attack with the profile: Club-tail. {@atk mw} range, 5 ft., +(Strength bonus + PB) to hit, one target. {@h}{@dice 1d6} + PB bludgeoning damage.
{@b Gastric barrier} – {@i This creature has a specialised digestive system that makes it particularly hardy.}
This creature has advantage on Constitution saving throws.
{@b Ink sacs} – {@i By squeezing specialised sacs on this creature's neck, it can spray ink from its mouth.}

As a bonus action, this creature may squirt ink at an opponent. Select a creature within 20 ft. It must succeed a DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition blinded} for two rounds.
{@b Nocturnal} – {@i This creature naturally prefers the dark and has very large eyes.}
This creature gains {@sense darkvision||dark vision} equal to its normal vision, or increases its {@sense darkvision||dark vision} range by 30 ft. It is generally only active at night.
{@b Telepathic cortex} – {@i A large bump at the back of this creature's skull houses an extra brain cortex.}
This creature is able to telepathically communicate with any other members of its species within 200 ft.
{@b Opposable claws} – {@i One claw on each hand is bent inwards, forming a thumb.}
This creature may interact with objects that require simple or complex movements, such as opening a door or using a trinket.
{@b Interlocking scales} – {@i Thick, tightly locked scales coat this creature's body.}
This creature gains resistance to piercing damage.
{@b Horned} – {@i Fused scales protrude from this creature's forehead or snout, forming pointed horns.}

If this creature moves at least 20 ft. towards a creature, it can use its bonus action to make a horn attack. If that creature is within 5 ft., it must succeed a DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB) Dexterity save or take {@dice 1d6} + PB piercing damage.
{@b Fusiform} – {@i This creature can tuck its arms and legs to its sides and adopt a fish-like shape.}
If this creature can swim, double its swim speed.
{@b Enhanced hepatocytes} – {@i This creature's liver is able to filter out any poisons almost instantly.}
This creature is immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition.
{@b Quick-witted} – {@i This creature can react quickly to changing situations.}
This creature has advantage on Intelligence saving throws.
{@b Elongated snout} – {@i The snout and nose of this creature is extended, giving it a much more powerful sense of smell.}
This creature has advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that involve smell.
{@b Dermal spines} – {@i Thick scales protrude from this creature, giving its body a spikey appearance.}
When hit by a melee attack, this creature can use its reaction to deal {@dice 1d6} + PB piercing damage to the attacking creature.
{@b Gelatinous saliva} – {@i Thick globules of slimy saliva drip from this creature's mouth.}
Attacks from this creature that involve its mouth reduce a hit creature's movement speed by 10 ft. (to a minimum of 5 ft., non-cumulative).
{@b Tonic immobility} – {@i This creature can feign death, falling on its back with its belly up and tongue hanging out.}

If this creature would be reduced to 0 hit points, it is instead reduced to 1. It feigns death, appearing dead unless it is inspected with a DC (8 + Wisdom bonus + PB) {@skill Investigation} or {@skill Nature} check (their choice). It may choose to exit this feign at any point.
{@b Fearsome roar} – {@i Powerful lungs allow this creature to let out a gaudy and terrifying roar.}

As an action, this creature can roar. Each other creature within 30 ft. must succeed a DC (8 + Charisma bonus + PB) Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of this creature for 1 minute. They may repeat this save at the end of their turn and on a successful save are immune to the effect for 24 hours.
{@b Automimicry} – {@i Strange patterns and growths make it difficult to determine where this creature's head is.}
If this creature would be critically hit, the attack is instead resolved as a normal hit.
{@b Sciurus tail} – {@i This creature has a large fluffy tail that it can flick rapidly.}
This creature is unaffected by temperatures as low as -20°C Celsius (-4°F Fahrenheit) and can communicate silently with any other creatures of the same species that can see it.
{@b Serrated denticles} – {@i The claws or teeth of this creature are jagged and saw-like.}
All melee attacks this creature makes deal an additional {@dice 1d4} slashing damage.
{@b Hereditary memory} – {@i Ancestral memories are encoded into this creature's DNA.}
This creature has advantage on Wisdom saving throws.
{@b Antlered} – {@i Multi-pronged antlers protrude from this creature's skull. It can swing them back and forth, slashing at foes.}

If this creature moves at least 20 ft. towards a creature, it can use its bonus action to make an antler attack. If that creature is within 5 ft., it must succeed a DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or take {@dice 1d6} + PB slashing damage.
{@b Pneumatisation} – {@i This creature has air sacs and chambers within its bones, making it much lighter.}
Half this creature's weight and increase its walking speed by 10 ft.
{@b Mana-infused cortex} – {@i A pale-blue glow around this creature's head reveals it has innate magical abilities.}
Select one cantrip of your choice. This creature knows that cantrip. Its spell save DC is (8 + Wisdom Bonus + PB) and spell attack modifier is (Wisdom bonus + PB).
{@b Bombardier gland} – {@i Bulbous sacs on this creature's body allow it to spit or secrete reactive chemicals that ignite when they mix.}
Add {@dice 1d4} fire damage to any attack made by this creature.
{@b Thin dermis} – {@i The skin of this creature is sickly thin and its veins are visible below the surface.}
This creature is vulnerable to piercing damage. Instead of increasing its CR with this mutation, decrease it.
{@b Waxy skin} – {@i This creature has a thick waxy coating on its skin.}
This creature is unaffected by temperatures as high as 40°C Celsius (104°F Fahrenheit). Reduce any slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage this creature takes by 2.
{@b Viperism} – {@i A soft tissue frill can extend from this creature's neck, and it can spit like a viper.}
As a bonus action, this creature may make one attack with the profile: Venom Spit. {@atk rw} range, 30 ft., +(Dexterity bonus + PB) to hit, one target. {@h}{@dice 1d6} + PB acid damage.
{@b Finned tail} – {@i This creature has a large fleshy fin on the end of its tail.}
While in water, this creature has advantage on Dexterity saving throws and can dash as a bonus action.
{@b Beaked} – {@i A keratinous beak sheathes this creature's snout, concealing its mouth below.}
This creature may add {@dice 1d6} piercing damage to any attack that involves its mouth.
{@b Bony frill} – {@i A broad bony frill projects from the back of this creature's head, allowing it to shield its body from attacks.}
Increase the AC of this creature by 2.
{@b Strong swimmer} – {@i This creature has powerful limbs and broad claws/paws/hands that aid it in moving through water.}
This creature gains a swim speed equal to 75% of its walking speed (rounded up to the nearest 5 ft.)
{@b Augmentative size} – {@i This creature is much larger than you would expect.}
Increase this creature's size by one stage, and its attacks deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage (of the same damage type that they normally deal), but -2 from any Dexterity saving throws.
{@b Hyper-bioluminescence} – {@i Rather than glowing dimly, for a moment this creature can flash an extremely bright bioluminescent light.}

Once per day as an action, this creature may produce a flash of bright light. All other creatures within 20 ft. that can see it must succeed a DC (8 + Constitution bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition blinded} for 2 rounds.
{@b Complex inner-ear} – {@i When other creatures would fall over, this creature is able to stagger and stabilise itself.}
This creature cannot be knocked {@condition prone}.
{@b Thick plumage} – {@i Particularly dense and thick feathers or fur cover this creature, giving it a puffy appearance.}
This creature gains resistance to cold damage.
{@b Xerophytic} – {@i Specialised fleshy flaps cover this creature's nostrils, and it has waxy skin or scales.}
This creature can survive without water for up to one week.
{@b Excessive myelin} – {@i This creature has a reinforced nervous system.}
This creature is immune to the {@condition paralyzed} condition.
{@b Frail} – {@i This creature appears thin and brittle.}
This creature has disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Instead of increasing its CR with this mutation, decrease it.
{@b Venomous} – {@i Horrible green venom seeps from grooves in this creature's claws and teeth.}
Add {@dice 1d4} poison damage to any melee attack made by this creature.
{@b Agile} – {@i This creature is slender and lean, able to move quickly on its feet.}
This creature has advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
{@b Dorsal wings} – {@i A small pair of wings or wing-like flaps extend from this creature's back.}
This creature knows the {@spell gust|XGE} cantrip (spell save DC (8 + Wisdom bonus + PB)) and is immune to falling damage, so long as it is not incapacitated.
{@b Gripping digital pads} – {@i This creature has rough pads on its feet that strongly grip surfaces.}
While climbing, this creature can dash as a bonus action.
{@b Sparse osteoderms} – {@i Dense bony lumps dot this creature's back and flanks.}
This creature gains resistance to slashing damage.
{@b Symbiotic spores} – {@i Unusual cysts cover this creature's shoulders. They can pop when disturbed, filling the air with a noxious cloud.}

At the start of this creature's turn, any other creature of a different species within 10 ft. of it must succeed a DC (8 + Constitution bonus + PB) Constitution saving throw or take {@dice 1d4} + PB necrotic damage.
{@b Rapid thermal regulation} – {@i This creature can flush extremities with blood to rapidly cool itself.}
This creature gains resistance to fire damage.
{@b Spermaceti organ (minor)} – {@i This creature can emit a deafeningly loud ultra-high-pitched sound.}

As a bonus action, this creature may perform a sonic attack. All other creatures of a different species within 20 ft. of it must succeed a DC (8 + Constitution bonus + PB) Wisdom saving throw or take {@dice 1d4} thunder damage and be {@condition deafened} for 1 minute.
{@b Pachydermatous} – {@i The skin and scales of this creature are noticeably thickened.}
This creature gains resistance to bludgeoning damage.
{@b Hyper-pigmentation} – {@i This creature's skin, feathers, spines, and/or fur are jet black in colour.}
This creature gains resistance to radiant damage.
{@b Alluring pheromones} – {@i This creature gives off a sweet, intoxicating smell.}
Once per day, this creature may cast {@spell charm person} at 1st level (spell save DC (8 + Charisma bonus + PB)) without components and without requiring a spell slot.
{@b Arboreal} – {@i This creature is adapted to climbing trees, with hooked claws on its hands and feet.}
This creature gains a climbing speed equal to its walking speed.
{@b Mana gland} – {@i Specialised glands on this creature's body allow it to infuse magical energies into its attacks.}
Add {@dice 1d4} force damage to any attack made by this creature.
{@b Dazzling plates} – {@i Large vertical plates line this creature's back that can produce sudden bright red colouration when flushed with blood.}
This creature has advantage on {@skill Intimidation} checks.
{@b Chitinous} – {@i Invertebrate-like plates cover this creature's flank.}
{@b Lithophagic} – {@i This creature is able to ingest rocks and stones for sustenance.}
This creature can sustain itself by consuming rocks. Any attacks involving its mouth deal an additional {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage.
{@b Binocular vision} – {@i Two forward-facing eyes allow this creature to easily track prey.}
This creature has advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that involve sight.
{@b Hoofed} – {@i This creature has single stub hooved/clawed feet.}
Increase this creature's walking speed by 20 ft. However, this creature is slowed to 10 ft. per round in difficult terrain (rather than speed halved).
{@b Enhanced cerebrum} – {@i A bulbous node on this creature's skull causes its eyes to protrude a little.}
As a bonus action, another creature within 60 ft. must succeed a DC (8 + Intelligence bonus + PB) Wisdom saving throw or take {@dice 1d6} + PB psychic damage.
{@b Fossorial} – {@i Scoop-like powerful forelimbs allow this creature to dig.}
This creature gains a burrowing speed of 15 ft.
{@b Hematophagic (minor)} – {@i As it injures its opponent, this creature drinks their blood.}
Whenever this creature deals damage with a melee attack, it gains {@dice 1d4} temporary hit points (temporary hit points do not stack).
{@b Macropod} – {@i With its unusually large feet, this creature is able to jump or rear up and perform a powerful stomp.}

As a bonus action, this creature may perform a Thunder-stomp. Every other creature within 5 ft. of it must succeed a DC (8 + Strength bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}.
{@b Hypermobility} – {@i With flexible limbs and a lean body, this creature is particularly fast.}
Increase this creature's walking speed by 15 ft.
{@b Electrocytes} – {@i Yellow domed pods of specialised cell clusters dot this creature's back, crackling with electricity.}
Add {@dice 1d4} lightning damage to any attack made by this creature.
{@b Pinnae} – {@i Pointed wolf-like ears protrude from this creature's head.}
This creature has advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that involve sound.
{@b Reverberating membranes} – {@i Specialised flaps of skin line this creature's flanks. It can vibrate them suddenly, producing small shockwaves.}
Add {@dice 1d4} thunder damage to any attack made by this creature.
{@b Regenerative torpor} – {@i A miniature hibernation allows this creature to recover rapidly.}
This creature may gain all the benefits from completing a long rest when it completes a short rest.
{@b Dynamic camouflage} – {@i The scales or feathers of this creature can change colour slightly, allowing it to blend into its surroundings.}
This creature has advantage on {@skill Stealth} checks.
Ocean/Deep Water, Jungle/Rainforest, River/Lake, Temperate/Conifer Forest, Island/Archipelago
{@b Hyena-like giggle} – {@i The constant cackling of this creature is unnerving.}
This creature knows the {@spell vicious mockery} cantrip (spell save DC (8 + Charisma bonus + PB)).
{@b Wader} – {@i This creature has webbed feet and thin ankles.}
This creature is not slowed by moving through shallow or waist-deep water.
{@b Hyperdontia} – {@i The teeth of this creature are particularly large.}
If this creature misses with an attack involving its mouth, as a reaction, it may attempt that attack again.
{@b Springy tendons} – {@i Frog-like spring-loaded limbs allow this creature to bound forward.}
This creature can jump up to 10 ft. further than it normally could.
{@b Seismic organs} – {@i Specialised sensory hairs and quills on this creature allow it to sense movement.}
This creature gains {@sense tremorsense||tremor sense} 30 ft.
{@b Volplane membrane} – {@i Broad membranes link this creature's front limbs and back limbs, allowing it to glide.}
This creature is immune to falling damage, so long as it is not incapacitated. While falling, it can move 1 ft. horizontally for every 2 ft. it descends.
{@b Chameleon-like tongue} – {@i In a flash, this creature can fire it's long, sticky, retractable tongue.}

As an action, this creature may make a ranged attack with the profile: Sticky Tongue. {@atk rw} range, 20 ft., +(Dexterity bonus + PB) to hit, one target. {@h}A creature hit by this attack is {@condition grappled} (escape DC (8 + Strength bonus)) and moved 20 ft. directly towards the attacker.

This creature gains a {@sense blindsight} of 20 ft.

This creature gains resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

Whenever this creature deals damage with a melee attack involving its mouth, the target is also {@condition grappled} (escape DC (8 + Strength bonus + PB)). This creature may also continue to attack while grappling a target, but may only use attacks that require its mouth against the {@condition grappled} target.
{@b Armour-plated} – {@i Extremely thick bony plates line this creature's body.}

{@b Grasping tentacles} – {@i Writhing tentacles protrude from this creature, trying to grasp their prey.}

As a bonus action, this creature may attempt to grapple another creature within 10 ft. of it. That creature must succeed a DC (8 + Dexterity bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition grappled} (escape DC (8 + Strength bonus + PB)).
{@b Winged} – {@i This creature's limbs have huge membranous or feathered wings.}
This creature gains a flying speed equal to its walking speed. If it can already fly, its flying speed is doubled.
{@b Flawless organism} – {@i Strong, fast, smart - the peak of evolution, everything is perfectly balanced.}
In addition to any other modifiers, add this creature's PB to any saving throws and ability checks.
{@b Enormous size} – {@i This creature is far larger than you would expect.}
Increase the maximum health points of this creature by 50%, increase its size category by two stages, and increase its CR by an additional 2.
{@b Draconic evolution} – {@i Bony spikes protrude backwards from the back of this creature's head, revealing its draconic nature.}

Exhale fire {@recharge 5}. As an action, this creature may exhale fire in a 30 ft. cone. Any creature in the cone must succeed a DC (8 + Constitution bonus + PB) Dexterity saving throw or take {@dice 15d6} fire damage. On a success they take half as much damage.
{@b Hematophagic (major)} – {@i Every drop of spilled blood is lapped up by this voracious predator.}
Whenever this creature deals damage with a melee attack, it gains temporary hit points equal to half of that damage (rounded down). Increase its CR by an additional 2.
{@b Elemental immunity} – {@i This creature is infused with a magical element, changing its colour accordingly.}

Select one damage type from lightning, fire, cold, poison, or acid. This creature is immune to that damage type and its feather/fur/skin colour changes to yellow, red, blue, purple, or green accordingly. Its attacks also deal an additional {@dice 2d4} of that damage type.
{@b Chromatic plumage} – {@i Iridescent feathers or fur shimmer with shifting magical energies.}

At the start of this creature's turn, you can select one of the following damage types: lightning, fire, cold, poison, or acid. Until the start of its next turn, this creature gains resistance to that damage type and one of its attack's damage changes to that type.
{@b Supernumerary} – {@i Additional back-up organs allow this creature's body to replenish venom and gland stocks more quickly.}
When you roll to recharge an ability for this creature, roll an additional {@dice 1d6} and choose the highest. If this creature does not have a recharge ability, reroll this result.
{@b Enhanced senses} – {@i Extra eyes, antennae, or multiple ears allow this creature to better sense its surroundings.}
This creature has advantage on {@skill Perception} checks and increase its passive Perception by 4.
{@b Chameleonic skin} – {@i Instantly shifting and changing scales perfectly mimic the colour of this creature's surroundings.}

As a bonus action, this creature can cast {@spell invisibility} at 2nd level on itself without components and without requiring a spell slot. It may do this a number of times per day equal to its proficiency bonus.
{@b Macro electrocytes} – {@i Giant protruding yellow sacs dot this creature's back, crackling with powerful electricity.}

The first time this creature deals damage with an attack each turn, add {@dice 1d10} lightning damage to that attack. This creature may also cast {@spell lightning bolt} at 3rd level (spell save DC (8 + Wisdom bonus + PB)) without components and without requiring a spell slot. It may do this a number of times equal to its proficiency bonus per day.
{@b Spermaceti organ (major)} – {@i This creature has a huge bulbous whale-like head, housing a powerful noise-producing organ.}

Sonic Scream {@recharge 5}. As an action, this creature may make a sonic attack. The first time it deals damage with a melee attack each turn, that attack deals a further {@dice 2d6} piercing damage.

table.name: Creature Names: Carnivores
intro: Just like in real life, in many fantasy settings animals are given colloquial names that differ from region to region. While we have given every animal in this book its real scientific name, you may want to use alternative names in your world. To help you come up with names, we've included a series of tables below.

These tables provide a prefix and suffix that you can combine with a verb to create compelling fantasy creature names. We suggest rolling or picking one-to-two prefixes, then a suffix, and finally a verb that combine to make a three-to-four word name. Alternatively, you can choose the words that you think best characterize particular aspects of the creature you are describing. Remember that a single species may have different colloquial names in different regions. Some example names include: Razor-clawed Slasher, Dusky-cheeked Hunter, Red Horned Crusher, or Gentle Cape Gorger.

variantrule.name: Taming and Domestication
entries: In this section we outline the rules for taming wild animals, as well as worldbuilding tools to help include domesticated animals.

Wild animals are difficult and often dangerous to tame. Instinct can override learned behaviour and it can take years to train an animal well. In a fantasy game setting, we want this process to be much faster and more involved, but still challenging. Below, we have outlined a process for taming wild animals. You may want to adjust these based on player power or the type of creature that is being tamed.

entries.name: Taming Rules
entries: Each creature with the Beast type has a Taming Score. This score is 0 unless otherwise stated by the DM. Once a creature has been subdued and is tied/chained/caged so that it cannot escape (but not {@condition restrained}), a player may attempt to increase that creature's Taming Score. Unless otherwise stated, they may attempt to do this once per day, as the creature will be unreceptive to multiple training sessions.

In order to make this attempt, the player must have appropriate food in an appropriate volume to feed the beast, as outlined in the Taming Food table below. The player then attempts to bond with the animal over the course of an hour. They must make a contested Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) vs Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check against the creature. Each success by the player increases the taming score of the creature by 1. Each failure by the player drops this score by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and the creature makes a single attack at disadvantage at the player attempting to tame it.

When that score exceeds the creature's proficiency bonus or CR (whichever is higher), the animal is considered tame and is loyal to the player/NPC (or team of players/NPCs) who tamed it. It will follow them unless commanded to stay.

items: {@condition Charmed} creatures make their {@skill Survival} check at disadvantage and cannot make an attack if the player is unsuccessful.
Dominated creatures automatically fail their {@skill Survival} check.
A player using {@spell Speak with Animals} has advantage and expertise on their {@skill Animal Handling} check.
